rules.statement: A feature turned on by a property or by the host's classpath never runs without what it needs (its module, its REQUIRED listener, its Redis connection): startup fails and names what to add. A module no feature uses needs nothing: a service behind a gateway (`cosec.pipeline.mode=gateway`) with JWT off, which wires no Redis data plane, starts without Redis although `cosec-cocache` is on its classpath.

rules.statement: The starter's startup checks run whatever spring.main.lazy-initialization says: every module check (STA-1), the actuator endpoint check (STA-2), the eviction policy check and monitor (SNP-3), the replica read check (RC1-47), the API key membership check (IDN-6), the pipeline mode check, the unknown property check and the control plane's own-authorization check fail startup under lazy initialization as they do without it, and the components that keep watching once the host runs (the eviction policy monitor, shadow reporting, control-plane maintenance, the listeners' metrics) start at startup. Each of them is a StartupTask bean, which lazy initialization never defers; no auto-configuration of the starter declares one any other way. A configuration none of them refuses starts under lazy initialization.

rules.statement: On every port a host opens, nothing the application serves answers without passing CoSec. A WebFlux application's management server (management.server.port different from the application's) is under the pipeline, as its application port is: its probes, and what it inherits of the application's functional routes; CoSec's own routes (the control API, the login routes) are not served there (CTL-69). A WebMvc application's management server serves only actuator's endpoints: a controller, a functional route, the control API and the login routes are not served there. A gateway's management server serves actuator's endpoints, and none of CoSec's own routes (CTL-69); the gateway's routes are served there only where Spring Cloud Gateway cannot tell the port apart (a random management port), and then under the gateway's filter. With one port, the probes are requests like any other.

rules.statement: When the application declares a CorsConfigurationSource (the bean of its own stack's interface; Spring MVC's own HandlerMappingIntrospector is not a declaration) and registers no CorsFilter or CorsWebFilter of its own, the starter registers a CORS filter immediately before the pipeline's on Spring MVC and WebFlux. A preflight (OPTIONS with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method) is then answered by that filter and is not decided: no policy, rate limit, blacklist, audit, decision event or metric sees it. An OPTIONS that is no preflight is decided as before; a request that is not a preflight is decided as before, and a refusal carries the CORS headers; an origin the source does not allow is refused by the filter before the pipeline. Without the bean nothing is registered and a preflight is decided as http:OPTIONS for an anonymous caller.

rules.statement: A host whose web adapter takes its caller from the `CoSec-Identity` header, which is a host in `cosec.pipeline.mode=gateway`, a host with `cosec.pipeline.caller=forwarded-identity`, or one whose web gate is an `IdentityGate` its application declared, fails to start when a hidden-method filter is on: `spring.mvc.hiddenmethod.filter.enabled=true`, `spring.webflux.hiddenmethod.filter.enabled=true`, or a `HiddenHttpMethodFilter` bean of the application's own, since the gateway decided the method of the request line and the host would run the one a form field `_method` names, which the gateway cannot remove from a body. The failure names the property or the bean and why. A host that decides on the credentials it verifies (`enforce`, `caller=credential`) is not affected: CoSec's filter runs after the hidden-method filter there (`PIP-19`).

rules.statement: A host whose web adapter takes its caller from the `CoSec-Identity` header (the three cases of `STA-6`) believes any such header it receives, and the header carries no signature, so the network is the boundary. It fails to start unless the operator states what can reach it, `cosec.pipeline.identity.only-gateway-can-reach` or `cosec.pipeline.identity.only-trusted-callers-can-reach` (`STA-9`) written `true` (any letter case, nothing else: absent, empty, `false`, `1` and `on` fail alike), with a message that says what the host trusts and that it contains mistakes and keeps the audit but does not defend against a compromised workload that can reach it, what must be true of the network (a NetworkPolicy, mutual TLS or a private network) and the exact lines to add. When it is set the startup logs one INFO line, not a warning. A host that takes its callers from the credentials it verifies needs none.

rules.source: maintainer decision 2026-11-19 ("要求显式声明"); IDN-27; RFC 0006 §5.3.2
rules.statement: A host that serves the refresh route (`cosec.authentication.login.refresh.path`) with the starter's own refresh and no `MembershipRefresh<RefreshTokenCredentials>` bean fails to start unless `cosec.jwt.session.memberships-on-refresh` is written `from-token` (any letter case, nothing else: absent, empty, `true`, `claims` and a padded value fail alike), because without a choice a refresh copies the memberships of the token it replaces and a removed role keeps working until the member signs in again, up to `cosec.jwt.session.lifetime`. The message says, in this order, what happens without a choice (with `cosec.jwt.session.lifetime` and `cosec.jwt.token-validity.refresh` as configured), the two ways to choose (a `MembershipRefresh` bean that reads the member's roles and attached policies again at each refresh, or the property), that `TokenRevoker.revokeSubject` ends a member's tokens at once in either case, then the exact line and a link to the page. With the property set the startup logs one INFO line with the session lifetime it implies; with a bean, nothing. A host that does not serve the refresh route, or whose application builds its own `RefreshTokenAuthentication`, is not asked.

rules.source: maintainer decision 2026-11-21 (the control-plane host's callers, "按你推荐"); RFC 0006 §7.3
rules.statement: `cosec.pipeline.caller=forwarded-identity` on a host that decides with policies (`cosec.pipeline.mode=enforce`) makes the web adapters' gate the `IdentityGate`: the caller is the principal the `CoSec-Identity` header states, believed under the operator's statement of what can reach the host, and the control plane, the snapshot and every other part of `enforce` are wired. The host verifies no credential: with `cosec.jwt.enabled=false` it holds no signing secret, issues no token and wires no token authenticator, yet its control plane still reads the revocations of an approver's token (`RC1-11`) from the token tables, which it wires for this caller. The two statement keys of `STA-7` are `cosec.pipeline.identity.only-gateway-can-reach` (only the gateway can reach the host) and `cosec.pipeline.identity.only-trusted-callers-can-reach` (the gateway and the services the operator names can); either satisfies the check, and the message names both. On such a host the web adapter does not decide a request, as in `gateway` mode: the gateway decided what came through it, and for a call that did not come through the gateway only the control plane's own authorization of each operation, as the principal the caller states, decides. A route of the application's own on such a host (the IAM service of the embedded deployment) is authorized at the gateway or not at all. A host with a service port (`cosec.control.http.service-port`, `CTL-58`) states `only-trusted-callers-can-reach`, since the port admits services: the gateway's key, `only-gateway-can-reach`, is refused beside it, naming the key to write. A host whose caller is the credential (`caller=credential`, the default) wires no `IdentityGate` and is asked for neither. Neither property is read on a Spring Cloud Gateway host: it fails to start with `mode=gateway` or with this caller, since a gateway decides on the credentials it verifies.

rules.source: maintainer decision 2026-11-21 (the control-plane host as an image, "实现排在 beta.6", merged into beta.5)
rules.statement: `cosec-control-server`, the control plane as an image (`platform/control-server`), is the starter with the control plane and nothing else: it decides with policies and takes its caller from the `CoSec-Identity` header (`cosec.pipeline.caller=forwarded-identity`, `STA-9`), so it starts only under the operator's statement of what can reach it, verifies no credential, and issues no token. It refuses to start with `cosec.control.enabled=false` (an application that is up and serves nothing: the gateway image is the read-only one), `cosec.jwt.enabled=true`, `cosec.api-key.enabled=true` or `cosec.authentication.login.enabled=true` (verification or a login that nothing on this host uses). Its probes are on the management port, outside CoSec, and its readiness group includes the control store's format indicator (`cosecControlStoreFormat`): a store not yet converted (`cosec-migrate repair-references`) leaves the instance unready, visible and named, and is never a startup refusal. It runs with `cosec.authorization.shadow.enabled=false`: the shadow reporter, the only writer of an instance's status, is not created, so a shadow window never waits for a control host and `propagation` never counts one.
